name: Give a five-minute speech without notes
blurb: A properly structured, well-rehearsed five minutes delivered from memory. It has a real finish line and a real audience, which is what makes it worth doing.
steps: Choose a subject you genuinely care about and can speak on with authority.
Structure it: a hook, three points each with a concrete example, and a close that returns to the hook.
Write it out fully once — to find the language — then reduce it to a keyword outline of about eight words.
Memorise the structure, not the words, using a memory palace with one image per section. This is what makes it sound live rather than recited.
Rehearse standing up, out loud, at least ten times, including at least three times in front of someone.
Film a run-through and watch it back for pace, filler words and hands.
tips: Memorising word for word is a trap: one lost word derails the whole thing. Memorise the sequence of ideas.
Rehearsing in your head is not rehearsing. Stand up and use your voice.
Write the first and last sentences verbatim. Those two you can afford to know exactly.
proof: You deliver the full five minutes to a real audience, no notes, staying within 30 seconds of time.
